name: Is not, and does not include, a webpage or webapp
frName: N'est pas et n'inclut pas une page web
description:
Web pages are the pages/applications which can be accessed through a web browser. These criteria apply to all web pages or applications regardless of their complexity.

EN definitions:

  • web page: non-embedded resource obtained from a single URI using HTTP plus any other resources that are used in the rendering or intended to be rendered together with it by a user agent (after WCAG 2.2 [5])

name: Is not, and does not include, a document (that is not a web page)
frName: N'est pas et n'inclut pas un document non-web
description:
Non-web documents are some of the most common types of ICT. The most common formats are Microsoft office suite files such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF, as well as stand-alone audio/video files, but many other formats exist.

EN definitions:

  • non-web document: document that is not a web page, not embedded in web pages nor used in the rendering or functioning of the page

name: Is not, and does not include, any software (even software that is part of a device) (web apps are not included here)
frName: N'est pas et n'inclut pas un logiciel non web qui fournit une interface utilisateur
description:
The provisions removed by selecting this option are specific to all non-web applications such as, but not limited to native desktop and mobile applications installed on a device.

EN definitions:

  • non-web software: software that is not a web page, not embedded in web pages nor used in the rendering or functioning of the page
  • open functionality:functionality that supports access by assistive technology

name: Is not, and does not include, any hardware (of any type) (This will also eliminate "stationary hardware" just below)
frName: N'est pas et n'inclut pas de matériel
description:
This option includes all physical hardware requirements from the EN 301 549 and only should be selected if you are sure that no physical hardware is going to be included in the project. Step 2 offers additional questions to consider to narrow down this category.

For example, hardware can include  buttons, keyboards, controls, wired/wireless phones, computers, access cards, kiosks, or other physical controls included in the ICT.

name: Is not, and does not include, any stationary hardware (i.e., no harware that stands on floor, the ICT does not contain its own booth, etc.)
frName: N'est pas et n'inclut pas matériel stationnaire
description:
This option is specific to hardware that is built into the environment. Examples can include, but not limited to, kiosks, terminals, physical controls such as buttons or knobs, photocopiers, printers, etc.

EN definitions:

  • terminal: combination of hardware and/or software with which the end user directly interacts and that provides the user interface

name: Does not include any closed functionality  (i.e., all functionality is accessible to assistive technologies)
frName: Ne contient ou n'inclut aucune fonctionnalité fermée
description:
This applies to ICT with functionality which does not allow access to assistive technology. This could be applicable to the whole ICT (Like in a kiosk/terminal ), or in secure systems which require programmatic access be restricted for specific features.

EN definitions:

  • closed functionality: functionality that is limited by characteristics that prevent a user from attaching, installing or using assistive technology
  • terminal: combination of hardware and/or software with which the end user directly interacts and that provides the user interface
